input:
This is a great late brunch option during the weekends when the big morning rush dies down after 1 pm. Usually there is no wait or 5 minute wait at this time. One big complaint is that they don't have an organized system for seating guests. The servers don't always greet incoming patrons (which should be required Waffle House-style) and they sometimes tell you to seat yourself (which can lead to one or two people taking up tables for 4) or they'll seat you (whenever they get around to talking to you). 

I've ordered a several different dishes at this point and they have varies from ok to awesome. The chicken wings and onion rings are just ok. The wings are either lightly dredged in flour or not at and then fried whole. They aren't really seasoned so the wings are pretty bland. The "onion rings" made of formed, chopped onions that are breaded. The chicken fingers were a bit over battered and dry. The smashwich (or whatever it's called) was pretty good: your choice of breakfast meat with hash browns and eggs in a hoagie roll, but unspectacular. The club sandwich is classic diner fare that is very well executed. The egg and omelette platters are a very good deal and dang tasty. The best thing on the menu is definitely the waffle. It's gently sweet, very crispy and covered in butter. So good!

The service is generally pretty attentive (once you're seated), the restaurant and bathrooms are very clean, the food is a good, tasty value
Improve this in GPT way:
This is a fantastic brunch option to consider during the weekends when the frenzied morning rush finally subsides after 1 pm. At this time, wait times are usually nonexistent or just around five minutes. However, one major setback is their lack of an organized system for seating guests. Ideally, the servers should adopt a Waffle House-style approach and greet incoming patrons without fail. Instead, they sometimes tell you to seat yourself, leading to situations where one or two individuals occupy tables meant for four. On other occasions, they will seat you whenever they finally get around to acknowledging your presence.

Over time, I've had the opportunity to try several dishes, ranging from passable to downright awesome. The chicken wings and onion rings fall into the okay category. The wings are either lightly coated in flour or not coated at all before being fried whole. Since they lack proper seasoning, they end up quite bland. The "onion rings" are essentially formed and breaded chopped onions. As for the chicken fingers, they tend to be excessively battered and dry. On the brighter side, the smashwich (or whatever it's called) is rather enjoyable – you have the liberty to select from a range of breakfast meats, which are combined with hash browns and eggs in a delightful hoagie roll. However, it isn't particularly extraordinary. When it comes to the club sandwich, it embodies the classic diner fare and is executed to perfection. The egg and omelette platters present an excellent value for money and are undeniably delicious. Nevertheless, the waffle steals the spotlight as the star of the menu. Its delicate sweetness, exceptional crispness, and generous smothering of butter make it simply irresistible.

In terms of service, it generally remains quite attentive once you are finally seated. Both the restaurant and bathrooms maintain impeccable cleanliness standards. Overall, the food offered is enjoyable and offers a great balance between taste and value.

input:
This is the biggest and best location for HMV in the city. The prices aren't any different from other stores but they do have a larger selection of gifting (figurines,mugs,blankets etc) as well as the largest collection of titles that don't fit into what is new and hot at the moment. Anything that they don't carry can actually be ordered in for you but I have to say staff here are not always the best at phoning customers to let them know when their titles are in so one should definitely keep their number by the phone to check in with them after a week or so.

The biggest selling point for me here besides the selection has to be the staff at the tills. It can get a little busy here but lines are always dealt with quickly and I appreciate that they don't push as hard as other locations to try and sign you up for a pure card. F.Y.I to anybody considering the pure rewards program the redemption items are not that great. It took me about a year of collecting just to accumulate enough points for a true blood key chain and when I got it it was placed in a bubble mailer and not even in it's original packaging. Needless to say when it came time to renew the card I opted out.

Anyways to sum it all up I will say for selection and speedy service these guys get five stars but the prices as well as the sometimes slow ordering process drop it down to a 3. Still worth checking out though if you have been on the hunt at smaller stores for a particular movie or cd.

input: Was on a mission trying to find the perfect coat for the Holidays. Found my idea of the perfect coat at Burlington but they did not have my size. Went to Target, bought a coat but ended up taking it bath. Was not my dream coat. Next stop Ross. The only coat in my size was a beautiful Bomber style jacket made of pleather. Bought it right before Christmas. Now it's a few days after Christmas and my husband Guy points out to me that the coat is really wrinkled. I go on line and look up every possible hack to get wrinkles out of pleather. They all fail miserably. I just went back to Ross with that coat, no receipt, no tags and asked to speak to the manager. The manager is a young male with dark hair and black framed glasses. I tell him of my plight. He literally says go find what you need, no problem. WOW! You won't believe it, but there was my Camouflage coat, in my size, hanging there waiting for me. Oh the irony! They exchanged my coat and after all that I ended up with my Dream coat after all. Thank you Ross Dress for Less. You will forever be my first choice for now on!
Improve this in GPT way:
In my quest for the perfect coat for the Holidays, I embarked on a mission. My search led me to Burlington, where I discovered the ideal coat that matched my vision. Unfortunately, my size was not available. Determined, I headed to Target and settled for a coat that turned out to be a disappointment. It was far from the coat of my dreams, and I ended up taking it back.

With hope still in my heart, I made my way to Ross, my last stop. Among the limited options, there was one coat in my size—a gorgeous Bomber style jacket made of pleather. Without hesitation, I purchased it just before Christmas. However, my joy was short-lived as my husband, Guy, kindly pointed out the coat's unfortunate wrinkles a few days after Christmas.

Desperate, I resorted to scouring the internet for every possible hack to remove wrinkles from pleather. To my dismay, none of them proved successful. Feeling defeated, I returned to Ross, armed with the wrinkled coat, but lacking a receipt or any tags. I requested to speak to the manager, who happened to be an insightful young man with dark hair and black-framed glasses.

Opening up about my plight, I explained the situation to him. Astonishingly, he reassured me with a simple statement, "Go find what you need, no problem." I was taken aback by his genuine willingness to help. Little did I know, fate had a surprise in store for me.

In disbelief, I embarked on another search through the racks, hoping against hope. And there it was, hanging right before me—the camouflage coat of my dreams, in my size, waiting patiently. The irony of the situation was overwhelming. It seemed that the universe had aligned, and destiny had rewarded my perseverance.

With overwhelming gratitude, I exchanged my coat for the one that truly fulfilled my aspirations. Ross Dress for Less, thank you from the depths of my heart. You have earned my unwavering loyalty, securing your place as my first choice from this moment onward.

input: Philadelphia, I love you.  Places like this remind me why.  We sat at the counter and watched the guys make the pizzas.  Our son hates cheese on a pizza and they had one already on the menu for him: The Marinara (oregano, crushed san marzano tomatoes, garlic, olive oil).  It was simple... but delicious. If you like real wood-fired pizzas that char the crust (a little blackened... in a good way), this is the place to go to.  Our other favorite pizza joints that rival this place are Lombardi's (NYC) and Grimaldi's (Brooklyn).  We all had a slice and were shocked at the lovely simplicity of it. Razor thin slices of garlic dotted the fresh tomato sauce.  My husband and I shared the Salsiccia (fennel sausage, roasted fennel, tomato sauce, mozzarella).  Roasted fennel on a pizza?  Brilliant. I cried a little.  No wait... I REALLY cried when we shared this cocktail: The Brooklyn (Dad's Hat rye, Luxardo cherry, white vermouth).  It says it serves one, but they brought it out in a cute little bottle and gave us each a glass...each with a hand- crafted giant square ice cube (hipster-cool) and Luxardo cherries.  Perfection.  We also shared a Rotolo (pizza dough, mortadella, ricotta, pistacchio pesto).  Those are crazy amazing.  I kept saying my husband could eat the rest... then freaking out and going back for another bite. He's lucky I didn't stab him in the hand with a fork to fight over the last bite (to be fair, he was the smart one who ordered it).  I could've eaten several of those and forgotten the pizza (although that was wonderful too!).  We finished with a little dessert... perfect little Italian cookies ("Cookie Jar" - pignoli, almond cookies, chocolate biscotti, pistacchio gnocchi) and I got an Affogato (fiordilatte soft serve with a shot of espresso).  The soft serve is Italian sweet cream... decadent and lovely... with rich espresso in a pretty little Italian mug.  I'm in Heaven here.  I know nothing about Vetri's other restaurants, but I'm checking them out next time I'm in Philadelphia!  By the way... service was great and friendly.  5 stars all around!
Improve this in GPT way:
Philadelphia, a city of culinary delights, always manages to captivate my heart. The remarkable experiences I've had here remind me why this place holds a special spot in my affections. During our visit, we settled into the humble counter seats, eagerly observing the skilled pizzaiolos craft their masterpieces. One particular creation on the menu, The Marinara, caught our attention as the ideal option for our cheese-averse son. With its simple yet divine combination of oregano, crushed San Marzano tomatoes, garlic, and olive oil, it proved to be a delightful choice.

If you appreciate the art of wood-fired pizzas, skillfully charring their crusts to an alluring shade of black, this is undoubtedly the establishment to visit. As connoisseurs of pizza, we hold their counterparts Lombardi's in NYC and Grimaldi's in Brooklyn in high regard. However, the delightful simplicity found in each slice we indulged in left us in awe. Thin slices of garlic adorned the vibrant tomato sauce, dancing on our taste buds with each bite. 

Seeking a touch of innovation, my husband and I decided to share the Salsiccia, a masterpiece featuring fennel sausage, roasted fennel, tomato sauce, and mozzarella. The audacious addition of roasted fennel on a pizza proved to be a stroke of pure brilliance. The flavors were so harmoniously balanced that it was enough to bring tears to my eyes. No, that's an understatement. Admittedly, I shed more than a few tears of joy upon savoring this astonishing creation.

Speaking of tears, they intensified when we were presented with The Brooklyn, a meticulously crafted cocktail comprising Dad's Hat rye, Luxardo cherry, and white vermouth. Though it was intended to serve a single individual, they served it in an adorable little bottle, accompanied by individual glasses. Placed within each glass was a meticulously handcrafted, hipster-cool, giant square ice cube along with Luxardo cherries, a true testament to perfection.

Intrigued by the unconventional, we also shared a Rotolo, showcasing pizza dough generously filled with mortadella, ricotta, and pistachio pesto. These bite-sized wonders were nothing short of mind-blowing. repeatedly, I insisted my husband should consume the remaining portion, only to find myself unable to resist taking another tantalizing bite. Had it not been for my restraint, I might have even resorted to using a fork to vie for the remaining morsel (although, to be fair, he was the genius who ordered it). The Rotolo was so extraordinary that I easily could have consumed multiple servings, almost forgetting the equally splendid pizzas we enjoyed.

To complete our culinary expedition, we couldn't resist indulging in a petite dessert; a heavenly assortment of Italian cookies known as "Cookie Jar" - featuring pignoli, almond cookies, chocolate biscotti, and pistachio gnocchi. Additionally, I ordered the indulgent Affogato, which consisted of fiordilatte soft serve accompanied by a shot of espresso. The soft servemade with Italian sweet cream, proved to be the epitome of decadence and refinement, blending harmoniously with the rich flavors of the espresso, presented in an exquisitely delicate Italian mug. It truly felt like a heavenly experience.

While I may be unfamiliar with Vetri's other culinary ventures, upon my return to Philadelphia, I am determined to explore them without hesitation. Furthermore, it is worth noting that the exceptional service we received throughout our meal was marked by genuine warmth and attentiveness. Without a doubt, this extraordinary dining establishment deserves a resounding five-star rating across the board.

input:
When giving friends from out of town a tour of the French Quarter, one can only expect they want some classic New Orleans dishes. I've been here a couple of times, but they were the ones that wanted to go, due to their lunch special. It's a nice, well know restaurant that offers a 17.00 lunch special that includes a soup or salad, entree, and the option for a 4.00 Bloody Mary or martini. I got the Bloody Mary and it was a great size for the price. It was spicy and hit the spot.
They text message you when your table is ready, so were able to walk around the quarter while we waited. Thank god a lot of restaurants are getting rid of the those buzzers that make you feel like you are under house arrest. 
We sat down to a beautiful table right by the open shutters. The servers, were ok. They were busy, but forgot a couple of things we asked for. It was still a great experience though!
I got the pork chop with red beans and the turtle soup. The turtle soup was one of the best I have had. The pork chop was cooked to perfection and the read beans were seasoned very well. It came with cornbread, but it was very dry. After this lunch at noon, I didn't find myself hungry till it was basically time for bed. It was a very generous portion and well worth the money.

Muriel's is a great way to get a classic, good quality New Orleans meal at a decent price. The location is spectacular, and the history behind the restaurant made for great conversation at the table.
Definitely check it out if you are in the Quarter!
Improve this in GPT way:
When taking friends from out of town on a tour of the French Quarter, it's only natural to treat them to some classic New Orleans cuisine. I've visited Muriel's a few times myself, but it was at their insistence due to their enticing lunch special. This well-known restaurant offers a $17.00 lunch special, which includes a delightful choice of soup or salad, an enticing entree, and the option to add a $4.00 Bloody Mary or martini. Personally, I opted for the Bloody Mary, and it was the perfect size for the price, with just the right level of spiciness to hit the spot.

One convenient aspect of Muriel's is that they send you a text message when your table is ready, allowing you to explore the French Quarter while you wait. It's a relief that they've done away with those bothersome buzzers that can make you feel like you're on house arrest. Once seated, we were lucky to have a beautiful table positioned near the open shutters. Although the servers were a bit occupied and forgot a few of our requests, it didn't detract too much from the overall experience, which was still quite enjoyable.

For my meal, I decided on the pork chop with red beans and the turtle soup. The turtle soup turned out to be one of the most exquisite renditions I've ever tasted, bursting with flavor. As for the pork chop, it was impeccably cooked to perfection, and the red beans were wonderfully seasoned. The only downside was the dryness of the cornbread that accompanied the dish. Nevertheless, the portion size was incredibly generous, and it kept me satisfied until bedtime.

Muriel's offers a fantastic opportunity to savor a classic New Orleans meal of excellent quality at a reasonable price. Not to mention, the location itself is truly spectacular, and the restaurant's rich history provided wonderful conversation at the table. If you find yourself in the French Quarter, I highly recommend checking out Muriel's.

input:
I ate here for the first time today.  The woman that works behind the counter is really friendly and offered to waive the minimum credit order amount ($7), since I work nearby.

The food itself is pretty average for American-Chinese food.  Nothing great, but not bad either.  My sauce was greasy, but the food in general doesn't seem to be (e.g. fried rice).  They do have some vegetarian options which are of the tofu variety as opposed to fake meat. 

I would go back since they have lunch specials that come with rice and either a drink, soup, or egg roll ($5.75).

EDIT: I got super sick after leaving this review, and I'm 99% sure it was food poisoning.  Will not be returning.
Improve this in GPT way:
I recently visited this restaurant for the first time today. The woman who serves behind the counter left a lasting impression on me as she was incredibly friendly. To my surprise, she kindly offered to waive the minimum credit order amount, which is usually set at $7, due to the fact that I work nearby. Her thoughtfulness and willingness to accommodate customers made for a pleasant experience.

As for the food itself, it can be described as fairly average for American-Chinese cuisine. While it may not particularly stand out, it is by no means bad either. The only issue I encountered was that the sauce I had was a bit greasy, but fortunately, the rest of the dishes, such as the fried rice, were not. Additionally, I appreciate that they offer a variety of tofu-based vegetarian options, rather than relying solely on imitation meats.

One of the main reasons I would consider revisiting this place is their appealing lunch specials, priced at $5.75. These specials come with a serving of rice and the choice between a drink, soup, or egg roll. It's a decent deal that adds value to the overall dining experience.

Update: Unfortunately, I fell ill shortly after posting this review and strongly suspect that it was due to food poisoning. Regrettably, I will not be giving this restaurant another try.

input:
Delicious! 

I wish they took reservations, but my friend and her fiance go there nice and early so that we could snag a seat inside (it was cold out!). 

We ordered the bianco salad ( to share between 2) and the western addition (to share between 4).

I thought the salad was tasty but nothing special, despite the white chocolate shavings. Cute idea, but not enough crunch or pizazz to make the salad seem really fabulous.

The pizza, however, was pretty darn good. We ordered it deep dish to try their special cornmeal crust and were pretty impressed. 
The crust tastes a little bit like cornbread, a little bit like pizza dough, a tiny bit like grease (the good kind) and a lot like YUM!

I don't know if it was the best pizza I've ever had, but it was very good. It would be even better if it were a tad cheaper, and didn't get so crowded! But definitely worth a visit if you're in the area!

input: A downtown without a bookstore is like a downtown without... I don't know I lost the metaphor. It's just sad is what it is. You may be surprised at all the books they have that you didn't even know you wanted. They also have a small selection of new books. If they don't have what you're looking for, you can order it. The one thing I don't really like is that the $1 children's books can be jammed so tightly that it's hard to look through them. The kids books are also arranged by color, which makes it harder for me to distinguish between titles as I glance through. Prices are excellent throughout, and the space is really nice. Check it out!

input:
They used to make an Amiga bowl that had an abundance of shredded grilled chicken on the bottom of a flour tortilla bowl, a layer of rice topped with grilled onions and peppers with a queso sauce drizzeled over the top.
Tonight there was no rice nor any shredded chicken, it had been replaced with chicken crisps. They are the outer parts of a grilled chicken breast with no moisture and very few of them.
Having met the owner in the past and having his wife wait on me I knew something wasn't right.
I explained to the waitress that this dish had changed and wasn't good! She politely offered something else. What to order...if they had modified a basic dish what was next?
To my surprise a male manager came out and "informed" me that this is exactly what they had been serving for 10 years and I must have either special ordered something or was mistaken.
I said this is not what they had served me for the past 5 years and I never had requested a special order before. 
I also asked what they had done to the phenominal soft tacos? They were usually served in a soft warm flour tortilla and had moisture and flavor. Tonight they were stale and crisp and the filing was bland.  Again he informed me I was mistaken while he held my order that had been sent back to the kitchen in front of me.
I apologized and said I didn't wish for anything else, thank you.
Another manager came out a few moments later apologizing and stated that they are unfamiliar with what I had ordered and would "special order" anything I wanted. I declined.
Apparently their cook walked out tonight and they were winging it.
Too bad it was a good place to get a good mexican meal.
Two thumbs down on Poblano's.

I have had pleasant experiences with the owner and his wife in the past, so I knew something was off. I explained my disappointment to the waitress, who kindly offered me an alternative. I was left wondering what I should order next, as it seemed that even their basic dishes had been modified.

To my surprise, a male manager approached me and insisted that they had been serving this modified dish for the past 10 years, suggesting that I must have either special ordered or been mistaken. Feeling adventurous, I had ordered the Shrimp with Candied Walnuts entree with brown rice while he ordered the Sesame Chicken platter. I like the idea of sharing food, but my food was too busy all on its own without adding something else to the mix. The brown rice was cold and very bland while the shrimp was overly sweet and I didn't feel like the candied walnuts and melon balls were complementary flavors.

The chocolate cake we had for dessert was amazing though; 6 layers of chocolate on chocolate. It was so sweet and rich, we ended up sharing a slice.

So to sum up, service was great, dessert was great, but the food needs some work. Sorry PF Changs, I just am not impressed.

One thing I will note (that our server told us) is that they are very big on catering to food allergies (especially gluten).

On a recent trip to Port Richey, I selected Holiday Inn Express for a couple of reasons.  The main reason was the option of two beds (as I was sharing the room with my brother).  The other reasons were:  price, vicinity to my aunt's home and complementary breakfast. 

My family and I typically stay at the Hyatt Place/House when we're traveling.  However, since it was just my brother and I, I figured we'd give Holiday Inn a shot. 

+  The staff were very friendly and helpful.
+  Free wifi.
+  Breakfast was very good, offering both hot and cold entrees. 

-  Sadly, the beds were WAY TOO soft.  It felt as if the mattresses were past their life expectancy.  As a result, I didn't really sleep well for most of my three nights there.
-  The a/c was hit and miss with the lack of reliable thermostat controls. 

There was a pool and hot tub, but since I didn't utilize either, it wouldn't be fair to rate them.  There also a small gym that I didn't use either. 

All in all, it was just ok.  Hyatt has spoiled me.

I must say, the friendly and helpful staff made our stay enjoyable. Not to mention, the free wifi provided a convenient way to stay connected during our trip.

One highlight of our stay was the breakfast. It offered a wide variety of both hot and cold options, satisfying our different preferences. However, there were a few downsides to our experience. The beds, unfortunately, were excessively soft, giving the impression that they may have surpassed their lifespan. Consequently, I struggled to sleep well throughout most of my three-night stay. Furthermore, the air conditioning was inconsistent due to unreliable thermostat controls, which was a bit inconvenient.

Although the hotel boasted a pool, hot tub, and a small gym, I didn't utilize any of these amenities, so I cannot provide an accurate rating for them.

In summary, my stay at Holiday Inn Express was satisfactory overall, but my past experiences at Hyatt have set high standards.

input:
do not eat here. my husband, two friends and i went out for restaurant week to marmont steakhouse on saturday, january 26, 2013; our experience was horrific.  the four of us ordered the crab bisque soup for our first course, it was cold and we sent it back to be reheated.  my second course was the calamari it was bland, fried too hard and rubbery.  finally two ppl from our party ordered the lobster ravioli for an entree.  it was not lobster ravioli but beef. i asked our waiter and one other waiter to please double check with the chef because this is not lobster, i expressed that i have not eaten beef or pork since 1994, and that it would make me ill. they both came back separately and argued that it was in fact lobster. another party of maybe 6 ppl ordered the lobster ravioli, they had the same problem and sent their dishes back to the kitchen too.  the server finally came over after i'd eaten two of the ravioli to apologize for the kitchens error and telling us that was in fact beef. 
i have been in the bathroom all day with diarrhea from the beef ravioli! the staff was very nonchalant about it and offered an insincere apology.
Improve this in GPT way:
My husband, two friends, and I had a disappointing experience at Marmont Steakhouse on Saturday, January 26, 2013 during restaurant week. Unfortunately, I cannot recommend dining here. Our evening was marred by several issues that left us unsatisfied.

To begin with, we ordered the crab bisque soup as our first course, but it arrived cold. We had to request it to be reheated. This lapse in quality set a negative tone for the rest of the meal. Moreover, the calamari I ordered for my second course was either improperly prepared or poorly seasoned. It lacked flavor, was overly fried, and had a rubbery texture.

The most egregious mistake occurred when two members of our party ordered the lobster ravioli as an entree. To our astonishment, it turned out to be beef ravioli instead. We immediately raised our concern with both our waiter and another staff member, emphasizing that we had specifically ordered lobster due to dietary restrictions. Surprisingly, they argued that it was indeed lobster, despite our insistence to the contrary. However, our doubts were confirmed when another table, consisting of approximately six people, experienced the same issue and sent their dishes back to the kitchen as well. Only then did our server offer an apology, acknowledging the kitchen's error.

Unfortunately, the consequences of their mistake were severe. Having consumed two of the beef ravioli before realizing the error, I have since been suffering from severe diarrhea. This is especially distressing as I have abstained from eating beef or pork since 1994, making this a significant health concern for me. The staff's indifferent attitude and insincere apology further compounded our disappointment.

In conclusion, our visit to Marmont Steakhouse during restaurant week was nothing short of horrendous. The cold soup, lackluster calamari, and the mislabeled entree all contributed to a truly unsatisfactory experience. Coupled with the indifferent response from the staff, it is clear that improvements need to be made to ensure the quality and accuracy of the food being served.

input:
I went here on a Wednesday night and, though it wasn't busy, there were no open tables without a reservation,  except the tall tables in the bar area. It still seemed to be a very quiet place anyway. 

The location is not attractive, the street is dark and mostly empty at night, but the inside is stylish in a masculine, refined sort of way; dark wood, low light, maps on the walls and prints of watercolors depicting old Missouri scenes. It was a great place for a quiet, intimate dinner. They've got a couple of TVs up above the bar. 

They seemed very well staffed, as if each table had its own server. 

The menu is one page but very intriguing, I had so many questions for our server about "what is this?" and "what is that?" and he was totally nice and knowledgeable about the menu items. He seemed nervous and unsure at first, but he was friendly and made sure to check on us frequently. 

We decided to split 3 small plates and a side dish between the two of us and, honestly, it was a little too much food for just two people. Perhaps we don't have hearty enough appetites.

Their menu is so varied and interesting, it's really all over the map in terms of seasonings and ethnic origins but the main focus seems to be rustic and warming - at least at this time of year. I have a feeling they may change it up from time to time. I'm sure you'll get things here you won't find anywhere else. The prices are very reasonable, considering the planning and good execution of the food. You'd certainly find more expensive, and less original places in Clayton and down town. 

We ordered the smoked trout, the venison hot dogs, the mini monte cristo sandwiches, and the french fries. 

The venison hot dogs and the smoked trout were fantastic and interesting. The french fries were very well made, and the dipping sauces delicious. I was so impressed with these that I was then a bit underwhelmed by the mini monte cristos. Since everything else there seemed to have a unique spin on it, I expected them to do something original here as well, but they were just like any monte cristo you might have. They were very tasty of course, but nothing new. 

With the food plus two draft beers, our total was $52.05 before tip and we were stuffed and satisfied. I applaud them!

input:
It is typical Broad Ripple charming spot. Small, trendy and bustling with activity. They do not take reservations. Which is somewhat annoying when you are traveling from another part of town. Whatever, we just had to arrange to arrive earlier than we would have liked to hopefully secure a table, which we did. When we arrived it was quiet and only several tables had guests seated. As our dinner progressed it became more crowded until every seat was filled. Nice lively scene except then you can not hear squat! It made dinner conversation difficult. Boo!!!! I think this could be an easy fix for them. 

Meal/Drinks:  The cocktails were creative and tasted wonderful. Our servers suggestions were pretty spot on as we enjoyed most of her suggestions. 

The guacamole was very good with the exception of the fact that my friend has a nut allergy and we asked to have them left off and of coarse they arrived with them on! They really weren't necessary in my opinion either as I don't think they add much to the dish. The reason I wanted to try this restaurant- The Harvest salad! We all split this as well and it was good. The combination of fruit and root vegetables was delish! The figs were so good and the herbed goat cheese mouse was a highlight on this plate!

Two of us ordered the Veracruz Trigger fish and the other ordered the Serrano Scallops and all of it was wonderful. The white sweet mashed potatoes were interesting! I am glad we tried them. The Veracruz sauce was wonderful and full of flavor. It was a lot of food though. Had we known we would have probably skipped one of the first course selections or split an entree. That'a ok though- lunch for today :)

We also tried the Tostones and Stewed Black Beans. Beans were very good, full of flavor! Tostones seemed very dry but maybe that is what they are supposed to be- this is the first time I have had them. BUT, dipped in the Stewed Black Beans they tasted great!

We passed on dessert as they had no gluten free, dairy free options. Delicia offers many options for restricted diets, which we loved. Just no dessert, which is probably better anyway-we were so full! 

Go, you will not be disappointed. Just go before 7pm on a Friday night to ensure a table.
Improve this in GPT way:
In GPT way: Broad Ripple is a charming spot, known for its small, trendy establishments that are always bustling with activity. The only downside is that they don't take reservations, which can be quite frustrating, especially when you're traveling from another part of town. Nevertheless, we made arrangements to arrive earlier than we would have preferred, just to secure a table, and luckily, we succeeded. When we got there, the place was quiet, with only a few tables occupied. However, as the evening progressed, it became increasingly crowded, to the point where every seat was taken. It created a nice, lively atmosphere, but unfortunately, it made having a conversation over dinner quite challenging. It's something they should definitely work on, as it could easily be fixed.

Now, let's talk about the highlight of the night: the meal and drinks. The cocktails were incredibly creative and tasted absolutely wonderful. We took our server's suggestions, and for the most part, they were spot on. The guacamole was delicious, except for the fact that they mistakenly included nuts, despite us specifically asking for them to be left off. Personally, I don't think the nuts add much to the dish anyway. The reason we were eager to try this restaurant was for their Harvest salad, and it did not disappoint. The combination of fruit and root vegetables was simply delightful, and the figs were particularly outstanding. The herbed goat cheese mouse was also a standout element on the plate.

For the main course, two of us ordered the Veracruz Trigger fish, while the other opted for the Serrano Scallops, and all of it was fantastic. The white sweet mashed potatoes were their own unique twist, and we were glad we decided to give them a try. The Veracruz sauce was packed with flavor and truly enhanced the dish. However, it was quite a large portion, and had we known, we probably would've skipped one of the first course selections or shared an entree. But that's okay, we'll just have leftovers for lunch today.

We also sampled the Tostones and Stewed Black Beans. The beans were bursting with flavor and were undeniably delicious. As for the tostones, they seemed a bit dry, but perhaps that's how they're meant to be. It was my first time having them, but when dipped in the Stewed Black Beans, they tasted great.

Unfortunately, we had to pass on dessert because they didn't offer any gluten-free or dairy-free options. However, Delicia, the restaurant we loved, does offer many choices for those with restricted diets. Besides, we were so full that skipping dessert was probably for the best.

Overall, I highly recommend visiting this place. Just make sure to arrive before 7pm on a Friday night to secure a table, and you won't be disappointed.

input:
This makes my 6th or 7th time to Jackson's in the last 2 years and I thought that after tonight's visit they deserved a review. 

I had the panini Reuben.  Panini was amazing. Great use of garlic. Loved the cut of the meat. Not stringy but nicely chinked in thin slices. Cheese was well melted throughout the mix of kraut and meat. Rye Bread was wonderful. Would love to have it as a staple in my house. 

Salad came out same time as sandwich which was not good.

Presentation was a little sloppy. 

Like every other place I have had a panini (except Panera where they do it right), the sandwich was served directly on a plate. Why don't they serve on a napkin? Particularly when they bring the salad out at the same time as the sandwich?  If the sandwich sits for more than a few moments, the bread gets soggy from the steam.  Nothing serious, but for the price, which is a little high, it seems lacking.  While the price is a little high, i think it is justified considering the food and drink quality. 

They have a great selection of wines and beers that are likely to fit any palette.  

Wait staff have always been friendly. But you can tell this is a place where people are expected to hustle. Sometimes short or even distracted the service can be lacking. 

The second time I visited was during a medium lunch rush and the wait time was 15 min to get drinks. My trip tonight it was about 8 min. For a sat night this is not bad. But not great either. My bartenders were awesome and never left me wanting (except for getting my salad with the main course).

Overall a good experience and I will be back.
Improve this in GPT way:
I wanted to share my thoughts on my recent visit to Jackson's, which marks my sixth or seventh time there in the past two years. After tonight's visit, I felt compelled to write a review.

First, I ordered the panini Reuben, and I must say it was absolutely amazing. The panini itself was delicious, with a great use of garlic that added a delightful flavor. The meat was perfectly cut, not stringy but thinly sliced, and it blended well with the kraut and cheese. The melted cheese was evenly spread throughout the sandwich. The rye bread was truly wonderful, and I wish I could have it as a staple in my own house.

However, I was disappointed with the timing of the salad. It was brought out at the same time as the sandwich, which was not ideal. The presentation of the food also seemed a bit sloppy. I've noticed that unlike Panera, where they serve the sandwich on a napkin, Jackson's serves it directly on a plate. Considering that the sandwich tends to get soggy from the steam if it sits for too long, I think serving it on a napkin would be a better choice, especially when the salad is served simultaneously. It's not a major issue, but for the slightly higher price, it feels lacking in attention to detail. However, the quality of the food and drinks justifies the price to some extent.

Jackson's offers a great selection of wines and beers that are likely to cater to any palette. The wait staff have always been friendly, although it's evident that they are expected to work efficiently. Occasionally, the service can be a bit short or distracted, leading to a slightly underwhelming experience. During one of my visits, which coincided with a busy lunch rush, it took about 15 minutes to get our drinks. However, during my recent visit on a Saturday night, the wait was reduced to about 8 minutes. While it's not terrible, it's also not exceptional. On a positive note, my bartenders were awesome and never left me wanting, except for the timing of receiving my salad alongside the main course.

Overall, I had a good experience at Jackson's and I'm definitely planning to visit again.

I went there for a pedicure and gel manicure.  It was my first time and the reviews was what enticed me. I loved loved Young, who did my pedicure.  She was very friendly and has a very positive attitude.  She took her time with my pedicure and was very thorough with the massaging (which was the best part). 

Unfortunately Young didn't do my manicure.   I had a gel manicure that needed to be soaked off.  The owner did my nails.  She first scraped my nails with the cuticle pusher, but when it wasn't coming off fast enough, she used the drill.  I was really worried as I didn't want my nails to be thin.  But I just let her do her thing.  I'm usually not picky so when she was working on my nails I didn't watch what she was doing until I realized after close examination she didn't fully take the old gel polish off.  
Not only that, the polish didn't go on smoothly, there's are noticeable bumps on my nail bed and the sides of my nails weren't even fully covered.  

I am so disappointed.  I love Young, but I don't know if I'll be going back due to my experience with my gel manicure.

input:

We brought my Mother-in-Law, who enjoys good food as long as it's not too weird.  I guess my wife is about the same, now that I think about it.  We tried three tapas plates; a three-cheese sampler, featuring feta, goat cheese and kasseri cheese, greek meatballs and pan-seared scallops.  We liked all three of these dishes.  The scallops were especially good - big and tender.   For tapas, they were pretty big portions, so keep this in mind.  The waitress suggested ordering one thing at a time, but we didn't heed her advice and ordered it all up front.   Two at a time would probably be a good idea.  Along with the tapas, we ordered a traditional Greek salad, which ended up being the lone clunker, surprisingly.  We just didn't like the dressing - too sweet for our tastes.  The gyro meat was fine, though, so maybe we'll just get a gyro next time.   One more thing:  The Spanish granacha (can't remember the label) was excellent for just $6 and a nice pour. 

Okay, now for the belly dancer:  She was cute and a good dancer, but I think this is just something that requires more alcohol on my part.  We did have a few laughs about it, though.  I opted not to get a dollar out to stuff in her skirt or whatever.   Fun but a little awkward. 

I've been to a few other Greek places in town that had better food, but for a night out, Momo's is definitely the choice.  We'll be back.

input:
This hotel was so terrible and I can narrow it down to 4 things:

1. The price: Expect to pay a lot of money from the second you arrive. They charge $35 per person for a round trip shuttle ride to the airport. Our room was roughly $275 a night. It's an incredibly large hotel that offers a nail salon, a Godiva Chocolate store, about 9 restaurants and a few bars. But you'll pay dearly for any of those things - like $2.50 for a small bottle of soda. The hotel is designed to keep you in there and they charge you $15 for a round trip shuttle ride to the downtown Nashville area. 

2. The service: We called the front desk and were on hold for 20 minutes. We went to the front desk and waited in line for an hour. We waited around to ask the concierge questions. And each time we got, "I don't know" as the usual response. The cleaning staff was extraordinarily loud and they actually shouted as they went down the hall at 6:30 a.m.

3. The name: They call this place a resort but that is, by far, a misnomer. This place is a convention hotel, period. It's horrifically loud at all hours of the day because they host about 3 conventions at one time. Our windows faced one of the courtyards and there is music pumping there 24 hours a day. The walls are thin and you can hear *everything* happening in the neighboring rooms. (eww!) If you want to relax at a resort, don't stay here because with all those convention people, loud cleaning staff, 24 hour music and thin walls you will only end up with more stress.

4. The size: It's no joke that you will get lost in this hotel. It's inexplicably large. And when it hits noon, you should already be in one of the few restaurants because they fill up FAST. With several conventions happening at one time, getting a "quick bite" is not possible here. And there's not really any place close by, either. You can walk over to the mall for some fast food but plan enough time for your walk - getting out of the hotel takes at least 5 minutes.

I'm sure glad I was there for a convention and didn't pay out of my own pocket for this ridiculous hotel.

input:
I waited a long time to finally try this place and I have to say I was let down a bit. I tried the mandatory Dan Dan noodles. They were very flavorful and not too spicy. Nothing mind blowing here just a really good lo mein or spicy pasta dish with virtually no protein more or less. Also had the scallion pancakes. I was just in Chinatown recently at a place I also reviewed (first person from Yelp to do so) and they were way better there. ( I highly recommend you try that place) These were more like quesadillas laying flat where as the other ones jumped off the plate and were so much more crispy and substantial. The last appetizer I had was the Wontons in Chilli oil. These were just not good to me at all and one bite was all I needed. Basically it is steamed Wontons in a bowl with the soup being the chilli oil. Just heavy heavy choking heat with very little substance or taste. Take those same homemade wontons and pan fry them with some chilli peppers and a nice light sauce and you have could a real winner but I digress. Finally we tried the Talapia Medallions . These were fried to perfection but there were some greens mixed in that I could not chew through and had to discard via the old napkin trick which to me is a bit of a deal/star breaker.

The service was very good and the atmosphere very nice but I wouldn't go out of my way to eat here again. All I could think about was how much more I prefer Cantonese style where its all about flavors and you can add heat as you like it. I'm sure I could find better authentic Szechuan cuisine that better suits my taste just not here. It feels very commercialized and Americanized. I prefer the hole in the wall places where I am the only caucasian in the place a heck of a lot more.
Improve this in GPT way:
I had been eagerly waiting to try this place for a long time, but unfortunately, it didn't quite live up to my expectations. The highlight was the Dan Dan noodles, which were packed with flavor but not overly spicy. While they were enjoyable, they didn't offer anything particularly outstanding, similar to a well-executed lo mein or spicy pasta dish, albeit with minimal protein. 

We also ordered the scallion pancakes, which, compared to a recent experience at another Chinatown restaurant (which I highly recommend trying), fell short. The scallion pancakes here were more like quesadillas lying flat, lacking the crispy texture and substantial nature that made the others truly exceptional. 

Next up were the Wontons in Chilli oil, and unfortunately, they simply didn't impress me. One bite was enough to make me realize they weren't to my liking. Essentially, they consisted of steamed Wontons in a bowl filled with chili oil soup – overwhelmingly spicy without much substance or flavor. I believe that taking those same homemade wontons and pan-frying them with chili peppers and a light sauce could transform them into a real winner, but alas, that was not the case here. 

Lastly, we tried the Talapia Medallions, which were perfectly fried. However, there were some greens mixed in that were incredibly difficult to chew, forcing me to discreetly discard them using the old napkin trick. This slightly tarnished the overall dining experience for me.

Although the service was impressive, and the ambiance pleasant, I personally wouldn't go out of my way to dine here again. Throughout the meal, I couldn't help but yearn for the Cantonese style of cooking, which prioritizes flavors and allows for individual preference in regards to heat. I am confident that I could find more authentic Szechuan cuisine elsewhere, better suited to my taste. This restaurant feels overly commercialized and Americanized, whereas I much prefer the hidden gem, hole-in-the-wall establishments where I am often the only Caucasian customer.

input:

Their mac and cheese remains my favorite side, and the addition of the very good coleslaw rounds out the experience.

I love the vibe of Kyber.  It usually pretty full, but they usually seem to have a table available for me (Yay!).  It is often loud, but never quite so loud that I wish it were quieter.  The staff is very knowledgeable, and happy to provide beer recommendations and taste tests of drafts.  They Khyber also manages to hit that sweet spot where I never end up being the most or least intoxicated person there!

Whether you go for the brisket, ribs, chicken, pulled pork, or a combination of these mouthwatering options, you won't be disappointed.

The atmosphere at Khyber is something I absolutely love. While it does get pretty busy, I never have trouble finding a table (hooray!). The staff is incredibly knowledgeable, always ready to provide beer recommendations, and even offer taste tests of their drafts. However, considering it's a specialty vegan place, I can't help but feel a bit underwhelmed. Maybe my expectations were set too high. Oh, and let's not forget about the green lemonade - it was far too sweet and lemonade-like for my taste.

If you're curious, I would still recommend giving it a try because many people can't stop raving about it. There are definitely some unique items on the menu that you won't find elsewhere. However, given the price range of around $10 for a lunch item, I wouldn't say it's absolutely mind-blowing.

Aside from the occasional Eggs Benny, whenever I go out for breakfast, I always order the same...eggs, bacon, hashbrowns and wheat toast with a side of salsa if they have it.

The hashbrowns were undercooked for my taste, so next time I'll ask for them to be crispy/well done. Everything else was quite good. Better than the Cajun Kitchen on Chapala, but not as good as the CK in Goleta.

Thankfully all of the special requests that I DID make were taken care of.

I'm super picky about my breakfast. 
Who am I kidding...I'm super picky about everything, lol.

Large portions(leftovers for tomorrow), super affordable(more so than CK), and loved sitting on their well shaded patio(no patio at CK).
There was one server taking care of 5 tables, she was great and very cheerful. No complaints about the service.

Terraza means balcony/terrace in Spanish and that's exactly why I would come here instead of other breakfast places that don't have one.

Next on the agenda...
Check out their lunch items.

In terms of breakfast, I always tend to order the same meal when I go out, which consists of eggs, bacon, hashbrowns, and wheat toast. If available, I love adding a side of salsa to complement the flavors. That's exactly what I went for today as well.

Additionally, the prices were very reasonable, even more so than the Cajun Kitchen. Another highlight was the well-shaded patio where I got to enjoy my meal. This is a feature that the CK in Goleta, unfortunately, lacks.

It's worth mentioning that the service was excellent, despite there being only one server attending to five tables. She was attentive and had a cheerful demeanor, so no complaints there.

With breakfast checked off, my next plan is to explore their lunch menu.

input:
I saw a deal on Groupon for Lee How Fook recently and after I read the reviews on Yelp, I was really excited to check this place out.  Unfortunately, I just didn't enjoy this restaurant and was pretty disappointed.

Lee How Fook is pretty small, but that didn't make it lose any points in my book.  I could see it getting really busy (especially since there are only about 10 tables available), so I would definitely suggest making reservations if you're going on a weekend.  The service wasn't bad, but when I asked some questions about some dishes on the menu, I had a hard time understanding what she was trying to say.  

Okay now to the main course - food!  For appetizers, we ordered the pan seared pork dumplings and sui mai.  Both appetizers were delicious and the dipping sauce was really good.  For the entrees, we ordered the sweet & sour chicken, pan fried noodle with shrimp, and pan fried noodle with beef and black bean sauce.  The sweet & sour chicken was awful - more sweet than sour - and the vegetables in it were really undercooked (pretty much raw).  (I do have to admit that I like things spicy, so maybe this dish just wasn't for me.)  For both pan fried noodle dishes, they were blah with a side of blah.  The beef dish was supposed to be spicy, but I just didn't taste any heat.  I left here full, but unsatisfied.
Improve this in GPT way:
In my recent exploration of Groupon deals, I stumbled upon one that caught my eye - Lee How Fook. Intrigued by the positive reviews on Yelp, I eagerly anticipated my visit to this restaurant. Regrettably, it failed to live up to my expectations, leaving me rather disappointed.

Although Lee How Fook may be considered petite, its size did not detract from its charm. However, with only about 10 tables available, I anticipated it could become quite crowded, particularly on weekends. Consequently, I highly recommend making reservations in advance. While the service provided was adequate, I did encounter some difficulties understanding the server when seeking clarification on certain menu items.

Now, onto the main event - the food! To whet our appetites, we opted for the pan-seared pork dumplings and sui mai. Both appetizers were delectable, and the accompanying dipping sauce was simply divine. As for the entrees, we decided on the sweet & sour chicken, pan-fried noodle with shrimp, as well as the pan-fried noodle with beef and black bean sauce. Unfortunately, the sweet & sour chicken fell short of expectations, leaning heavily towards sweetness and lacking the tanginess I anticipated. Moreover, the vegetables within the dish were severely undercooked, bordering on raw. Admittedly, my preference for spiciness may have influenced my dissatisfaction with this particular dish. I finally made it to Farmhaus last Saturday, and it was worth the wait.  

As expected for a weekend, it was crowded.  We arrived about 15 minutes early and had to wait on the bench back by the bathrooms for a few minutes.  However, as I said, we were earlier than they anticipated, and they got us to the bar as soon as seats opened up.  They wisely gave us a copy of the menu to be prepared once we were seated, and we did indeed plan our entire meal in advance.  This was helpful, because we were actually seated about 20 minutes late, and I was about to eat the menu itself as I drooled over the descriptions!  

The smoked fish dip and escolar with prawns were fantastic- the standouts of the meal.  The mushroom salad and tapenade were also very good.  The meatloaf was good, but a little on the dry and bland side.  I wanted to get the nachos, but there were no other takers in my group....next time....

Service was good.  It was a bit shaky at times, but it was slammed the whole time we were there and that small space must be tough to work in.  

I would love to go back and check out their blue place special lunches...I have heard amazing reviews.  I think I will head back for dinner when there is outdoor seating, as I think that would add to the experience.

I was so disappointed when this opened; I was hoping for Nashville's first real authentic Greek restaurant (Athens notwithstanding).  This isn't Greek; it isn't even Mediterranean. It's pseudo-Americanized versions of Mediterranean classic cuisine. The corporate chefs got so many things wrong:  Skordalia is a classic Greek dip made out of potatoes and garlic (not bread).  Avgolemono is chicken soup with egg, lemon and rice -- not this thin, awful broth they are currently serving. If one wants true Greek cooking, one should go to Greektown in either Detroit or Toronto. 
Just say no.
Improve this in GPT way: I was extremely let down by the opening of this restaurant; my expectations were high for Nashville's first authentic Greek eatery (excluding Athens, of course). Unfortunately, it falls short of being truly Greek or even Mediterranean. Instead, it serves pseudo-Americanized versions of Mediterranean dishes. The corporate chefs made numerous mistakes: for instance, skordalia should be a traditional Greek dip made with potatoes and garlic, not bread. Additionally, their version of avgolemono is far from the authentic chicken soup with egg, lemon, and rice; it's a disappointingly thin and unpleasant broth. For genuine Greek cuisine, it would be best to visit either Greektown in Detroit or Toronto. I strongly advise against choosing this establishment.

input:
Looking for a delicious New Year's Day brunch was hard this year in New Orleans. We didn't want to wait in line and wanted instant gratification. Although we may have felt tired, my bf and I were appropriately dressed to go to Mr. B's. As soon as we walked in, I felt transported into a different world. Jazz music was playing and I felt at home. 

First of all, I could not have been more grateful for the fresh loaf of bread we were given. We devoured it in a matter of minutes. Then came the gumbo ya-ya. It was spicy and savory and everything I expected from a gumbo. Finally came the bbq shrimp. We had been warned that these shrimp did come with their heads and tails on. Bibs were placed around our necks and we were off. The shrimp were some of the most rich and delicious ones I have ever tasted. The sauce they were served with was divine. Although it was messy, there is no other dish on the menu I would have traded for this.

Overall, service was friendly and quick at Mr. B's. The food was delicious, although a little pricey. Definitely try the brunch if you are able to.

input:
I've been here twice now and sampled a bunch of what they have to offer - I feel like what you order will really dictate how much you like this place.  i.e. they do some things great and other things just so-so.

The two things I will surely go back for more of is the Sausage and Pepper Pizza (capitalized - because I mean business) and some sort of puff pastry that has a white cream in the middle - I'm sure it has a name but it escapes me.  The pizza was perfectly flavored and the sausage/peppers had a nice kick to it.  Im sure it would make for great leftovers but unfortunately (fortunately?) for me it was gone well before it found the refrigerator.  The cream puff cream was just awesome - couldn't pin-point the flavor (vanilla?) but I would prefer it to top every dessert I get from this point forward.

I also got a bunch of the other sweets (salted brownie, blondie, red velvet crumb-cake) and a few bagels.  All were good, but not great.  Was pleasantly surprised by the wheat everything bagels - whole wheat bagels usually suck.

What I didn't really like was the pepperoni pizza.  It was pretty bland for my liking - in complete contrast to the sausage and pepper pizza - and the pepperoni was pretty sparse. I also didn't like being told 25 minutes, showing up in 25 minutes and then standing there for 25 minutes waiting for the pizza.  The small shop + no chairs = awkwardly standing there for almost a half hour.  

Since it's close to me and has so many tasty looking treats yet to try - I'll surely be back.  Hopefully I'll get more 'great' than 'so-so'.
Improve this in GPT way:
In my experience, I've visited this place twice and had the opportunity to try a variety of their offerings. It seems that your enjoyment of this place largely depends on what you order. Some items are executed exceptionally well, while others are just average.

Two items that I highly recommend are the Sausage and Pepper Pizza (yes, it's so good that I have to emphasize it) and a delectable puff pastry filled with a creamy white center. I can't recall the exact name of the pastry, but its taste is unforgettable. The pizza is perfectly seasoned, and the combination of sausage and peppers gives it a delightful kick. I had high hopes of savoring leftovers, but unfortunately (or fortunately?) it disappeared long before it could find its way into the refrigerator. The cream filling in the puff pastry was absolutely divine, though I couldn't quite pinpoint the exact flavor (perhaps vanilla?). I would personally love to have this cream topping every dessert I indulge in from now on.

I also tried a variety of other treats, including a salted brownie, blondie, red velvet crumb-cake, as well as a few bagels. While they were all good, they didn't quite reach the level of greatness. However, I was pleasantly surprised by the wheat everything bagels. As someone who generally finds whole wheat bagels lacking in flavor, these ones proved to be an exception.

On the flip side, the pepperoni pizza left much to be desired. It lacked the bold flavors present in the sausage and pepper pizza and seemed quite bland. Moreover, the pepperoni was disappointingly sparse. Another aspect that didn't sit well with me was the wait time. Despite being told it would take 25 minutes, I arrived on time only to find myself waiting for an additional 25 minutes. The lack of seating in the small shop made for an awkward experience, as I had to stand there for nearly half an hour.

However, due to its proximity and the multitude of enticing treats yet to be tasted, I will definitely give this place another chance. Hopefully, my next visit will yield more "great" experiences than "so-so" ones.

My girlfriends and I ate at the Creole House for dinner. Our decision to dine here was largely based on the fact that it was pouring raining and this restaurant is next door to our hotel. We started with the bacon garlic oysters and jumbo buffalo wings. The bacon garlic oysters were average, at best. The oysters were overpowered by the cheese and bacon, which was disappointing. The buffalo wings were pretty good and seasoned well. For entrees, we ordered: 1) jumbalaya pasta, 2) blackened red fish and 3) canal street red fish. The jumbalaya pasta lacked flavor and was our least favorite (would not order again). The blackened red fish was just okay and the skimpy side of sautéed veggies (spinach, tomatoes, mushrooms) were VERY salty (would order again as a LAST resort). The canal street red fish wasn't great but my friend would order it again. Her biggest complaint was that it had very little garlic sauce. We also ordered paddle boat drinks, which tasted good but were more juice vs alcohol (had to order an extra shot).

So, overall, we were underwhelmed with the food, making it a solid 3 stars. On a positive note, our server, Alexander, was great...very hospitable and tried his best to make sure we were satisfied.

Oh well......

input:
3.50 stars.  

Gabby's wasn't open.  I knew that.  Neither was Rotier's.  But my handy Yelp app had assured me that Fido's was open.  Imagine the disappointment when I realized there was a very real possibility that no burgers would happen on this trip down to the Deep South.  Would I really have to wait two more weeks when I would find solace in East Texas?   

"We can try Burger up," I mentioned.  

"Why don't you just call them?" hissed the appropriately nicknamed Viper.  

True.  We didn't have to keep driving around aimlessly.  So I call Burger Up, and a very pleasant, sweet voice assures me they are indeed open.  

Viper: "What was her name?  She sounded hot."
  
Me: "Paige."

Viper: "Yeah, she's definitely hot.  Have you ever met an unattractive Paige?"

Me: "Good point.  At least we have that going for us."

Paige was indeed attractive, but this review isn't about a photogenic individual who happens to work at Burger Up.  It's about what ended up being a visit to our fourth choice for burgers in Nashville.  

Burger Up follows a national trend towards upscale burgers.  My particular order consisted of a medium rare patty served with aged cheddar, Benton's bacon (very good), and ketchup served on an artisan bun.  Basically, it was a gussied up bacon cheeseburger, but it was a rather tasty one.  My major complaint is that I wish the actual meat itself exhibited more flavor.  Having said that, the burger was cooked properly and the flavors worked well together.  I ordered some wilted spinach on the side (mediocre) and truffle fries.  Let's talk about those truffle fries for a bit.  I know more people are apparently into the sweet potato fries here, but I think they are missing the boat.  Burger Up's truffle tries have pleasant aroma, taste great, and are the perfect texture for soaking up oil.  If you are on a diet, it is true you should skip these delightful fries.  But if that were the case, why are you at a burger joint in the first place?  Seriously, if you get nothing else out of my review, please do yourself a favor and order the truffle fries.  

Burger Up also boast an interesting beer menu with semi-obscure breweries from the Deep South included in the list.  I tried a pecan-infused amber from Mississippi - not bad.  I could imagine Burger Up could be a decent place to drink for a bit after eating.  

If I attended Vanderbilt, I would probably go here on a moderately frequent basis.  If you want a change from the dive bar hamburger, Burger Up is a decent change of pace.

Worn down signs intrigue me.  I had biked passed 16th Street Seafood a ton of times, always wondering what was going on inside.  Now I know the answer, and the answer is- not much. At least in terms of decor. There is a gumball machine, 2 empty candy machines, plus a counter to order at and that's pretty much it. Also absent was the plethora of seafood over ice you would hope to see at a place specializing in seafood. There were some frozen crab cakes, breaded fish fillets, clams, and crabs- but not else. Still, I threw caution to the winds of Tasker Street and put in an order.

I didn't want to go for fried seafood, so the sandwiches and platters were out.

I got a large order of mussels in butter and garlic sauce ($9.50). Mussels are one of those things I like making at home, but it is way too hot for that right now. . My main complaint is that the order came with an unacceptable amount of closed shells - 9!   It was still a good sized order with a big piece of bread to dip in the unexpectedly spicy, broth. As the place is to-go only- they know how to wrap up messy seafood orders, nothing was spilled.

Remember when I said I didn't want anything fried, well that's not ever actually true. So I ended up sneaking in 2 fried shrimps. Not bad, but not worth $1.25 each.

Animo juice is the best find in Haddonfield (after the Hadrosaurus, of course!)

Animo started with juice.  Not frozen juices with sorbet & yogurt added.  Real juice.  

Their menu has expanded & they now call themselves "Animo Juice & Burrito Bar!"  The burrito menu features 10 burritos, all under $10, f my favorite the "Haight & Ashbury" is stuffed with rice, beans, meat/roasted veggies, cheese, lettuce, tomato, guacamole & sour cream.

Not that hungry, have a 'petito', a small version of the burrito, averaging $5.  Porky & Petunia - the name is as cute as the petito is yummy:  shredded lettuce, pulled pork & pineapple salsa.  

A breakfast petito & Animo MD juice destroy any hangover.  The MD is juiced greens, carrot, orange, apple, kiwi, banana & spirolina.   My BF loves the Chilly Palmer:  Acai, apple, banana, yogurt & flax seed.  

For a happy belly add or substitute the perfectly cooked quinoa to any dish.  The Border Salad is a perfect example: lettuce, guac, pico de gallo, cheese, tortilla chips, cilantro lime vin, & sub quinoa for meat.   

Fiber-full signature juices, frozen whipped bananas, sliced fresh wheat grass (cheaper than Jameson!) & yogurt/granola bowls!  

The city's juice bars have something to learn from Animo.

input:
This is my favorite in Delaware.  The menu is simple and perfectly executed.  Rolls are reasonably priced, artfully made and are PACKED with fish!  I do believe they use flash-frozen sashimi grade fish, but the color, texture, taste and smell are perfect.  Easily the best spicy tuna I have ever had.  I think the secret is the kewpie mayo along w/ the right amount of sriracha and sichimi powder.  Frankly, I can't get enough of this place and have at times, eaten it every day for lunch for weeks.  I've gone as far as to pick it up for dinner AFTER having had it for lunch. Their introduction of short-grain brown sushi rice has been great!

The Sushiman, YC Park is amazing to watch.  I've seen him skin a cucumber with a sword-like sushi knife in no time flat, in a single ribbon and then continue to shave it into a nori thin sheet for his tuna naruto roll roll.  The temaki are as big as a carnival iced cream cone.  You can barely finish one of them, there is so much fish in there.  The nigiri are beautiful.  Uniform pieces of fresh fish, perfectly perched on the best sushi rice I've ever had (just the right amount of vinegar and sugar).

Skip the newly opened Kooma.  Save Mikimotos for a night out, but go to Tokyo for lunch!  The owners are lovely, so support them in this tough economy.  If you must eat sushi, eat it here!

Why not 5 stars?  I have to save it for places that serve the local fresh fish, plucked out of the water that morning.  Let me know if you find a place that does!
Improve this in GPT way:
In Delaware, there is a place that truly stands out for me - it's my favorite. The simplicity and flawless execution of their menu never fail to impress. The rolls they serve are not only reasonably priced, but they are also artfully crafted and filled generously with fish. Though I suspect they may use flash-frozen sashimi grade fish, the color, texture, taste, and aroma are impeccable. In fact, their spicy tuna roll is hands down the best I've ever had. I believe the secret lies in their perfect combination of kewpie mayo, sriracha, and sichimi powder. I can't seem to get enough of this place, and there have been times where I've indulged in their sushi every single day for weeks. I've even gone to the extent of picking up dinner from there after already having it for lunch. Their addition of short-grain brown sushi rice has been a welcome innovation.

The Sushiman, YC Park, is truly a marvel to watch. I've witnessed him skillfully skin a cucumber with a sword-like sushi knife in a matter of seconds, creating a single ribbon that he then transforms into a delicate sheet of nori for his tuna naruto roll. The temaki they serve are as large as carnival ice cream cones, packed to the brim with an abundance of fish. One is barely able to finish a single cone due to its generous portions. The nigiri is nothing short of beautiful, with each piece of fresh fish perfectly balanced on top of the best sushi rice I've ever tasted - a delightful harmony of vinegar and sugar.

While I highly recommend skipping the newly opened Kooma and reserving Mikimotos for nights out, make sure to visit Tokyo for lunch! The owners are not only delightful but supporting their establishment in these challenging times is crucial. If you have a craving for sushi, this is the place to satisfy it.

However, I must reserve my five-star rating for places that serve locally caught fish, freshly plucked from the water that very morning. If you come across such a place, please do let me know!

We went on a non typical day, school year mid week, so we had the luxury of being only a handful of people there  Therefore, my review may not be representative of a typical visit. 
Arrived at opening and found the off season price within reason. Bathrooms and water park were immaculate. The lifeguards were attentive and friendly. 
A star was lost because I found the water and air temp to be a tad too cold. The park was smaller then other indoor water parks I've been to. Only two big slides, one group slide, a couple of younger kids areas, lazy river and a simulated surf area. They would periodically close the big slides in order to open the surf area, for lack of staffing. A minor annoyance since that is why we were there. 
I can see how people  would be upset paying more and sharing the park with hundreds of others. But I think if your timing is right, you could have an enjoyable afternoon.
We did save money by using our AAA card. Could have saved more as it was my sons birthday month, but I didn't have proof on me.

Upon our arrival at the park's opening, we were pleased to find that the off-season price was reasonable. Furthermore, both the bathrooms and water park itself were maintained to a high standard of cleanliness. The lifeguards on duty were diligent and friendly, ensuring our safety throughout our time there.

However, it's worth mentioning that I deducted one star from my overall rating due to a couple of minor issues. Firstly, I personally found the water and air temperature to be slightly colder than preferred. Secondly, compared to other indoor water parks I've visited, this one seemed to be smaller in size. It featured only two large slides, one group slide, a few areas designated for younger children, a lazy river, and a simulated surf area. Occasionally, they would close the big slides in order to open the surf area due to inadequate staffing. This was a minor inconvenience since riding the slides was our main reason for visiting.

It's important to acknowledge that on busier days, with larger crowds and higher prices, some visitors may feel disappointed. However, I believe that with proper timing, one can still have an enjoyable afternoon at this water park. 

Additionally, I would like to mention that we were able to save some money by utilizing our AAA card. Unfortunately, I didn't have proof of my son's birthday month with me, which could have potentially led to further savings.

Overall, based on our unique experience, I would recommend this water park if you have the opportunity to visit during a less crowded time.

input:
I normally wouldn't think Greek food for brunch or lunch; I'm way more of a traditional American-style brunch kind of guy.  But when my friends suggested to meet them here for brunch this past weekend, I trusted their better judgement.  In the end, I'm glad I did.  This cozy Center City spot not only serves an amazing (and dare I say, a contender for the best) brunch in Philly, the staff really make you feel at home.  They really know how to wow their patrons: fresh food, delightful presentation, and so many delicious sounding choices it's hard to choose which dish you want from their one page menu for mains.

Their specialty, and they're not shy to tell you, is the Cyprus Breakfast.  It's a mediterranean twist on the classic combination of eggs, meat, and starch.  The plate comes out with two sunny-side up eggs, fried in olive oil and garnished with fresh parsely.  It's served alongside a grilled slice of lounza (Greek ham), two pieces of salty, crisp fried halloumi, warm bread, and tomato, cucumber, and onion salad.  The menu also features a spread of other traditional Greek, Mediterranean, and Middle Eastern specialities: Avgolemono, Moussaka, Pastitsio, Shaksouka, and Malohwa to name a few.  They even serve Greek Coffee and Frappes!

The service may be a little over-attentive in an attempt to make you feel more than welcome, but it's much appreciated, especially when other restaurants fail to put as much effort into the service as they do the food.  One other tip: reservations are highly recommended, if not required.  Because of Kanella's small space, getting a table at brunch is nearly impossible if you're not on the list.  But if you can score seats here for brunch, then expect nothing less than a stellar way to start your weekend morning (or recover from last night's activities).  Can't wait to come back and try out the dinner menu.

The service here may be slightly over-attentive, as the staff goes out of their way to ensure you feel more than welcome. One small piece of advice: make sure to book a reservation ahead of time, as securing a table for brunch can be nearly impossible without one. input:
One of the absolute best places to see a game in the entire country!

Get there early or if it's a blowout, stroll around the park. There are tons of interesting places to eat & drink (including a rooftop bar). Tickets are still amazingly reasonable even after all the success the Phils have had in recent years particularly when compared to the NY parks.

I used to go more often before the team became so prominent (right after the park opened), and I sat all over the joint. Not really anywhere I wouldn't recommend. The outfied is a great option. 

After starting with a 17 game pack many years ago & then buying season tix a few years back (which my company still has), the staff was great about recommending sections that would avoid direct sunlight , etc. (3rd base field level is awesome).

If you are visiting or considering a trip, don't buy the negative publicity about the Philly fans. The crowds are great. Sure, you have idiots and maniacs like you do at any park and for any professional sporting event, but they are by far the minority and Citizens Bank Park is policed pretty well for nonsense. 

I was once with a group of guys & we stood out in one of the open standing areas between 3rd base & the left field wall the whole night. At one point a very nice officer politely asked us not to curse because there were families around. We we were far from out of control, and we all thought that was pretty cool... so we had fun with some occasional lighthearted banter with the officer for the rest of the night.

Don't expect to be sheltered with your kids like you would be in your own living room, but there's no teens running onto the field getting tazed every night nor are there drunk idiots throwing up on people. 

It's a great atmosphere, a wonderful park & still a very fun team to watch.

I became a loyal fan after starting with a 17-game pack many years ago, eventually upgrading to season tickets which are still held by my company. The attentive staff always went above and beyond, recommending sections that offered shade to shield us from direct sunlight. I must admit, the field-level seats along the third base line are nothing short of awesome.

Now, if you're a first-time visitor or contemplating a trip, let me assure you that you need not pay heed to the negative publicity surrounding Philly fans. The crowds are electric and spirited. While it's true that you may encounter a few troublemakers or overly passionate enthusiasts, they are undoubtedly the exception rather than the rule. Citizens Bank Park is well-policed, ensuring a safe and enjoyable experience for all.

I recall an incident where my friends and I spent the entire evening standing in one of the open areas between third base and the left field wall. The atmosphere at Citizens Bank Park is simply incredible, the park itself is nothing short of wonderful, and watching the Phillies play is an absolute delight that shouldn't be missed.
