So we arrived an hour early and had drinks in the lobby while the piano man played beautifully. The bartender was a bit slow at first but kept us well tended. 
Our table in the corner against the glass was ready early and we enjoyed watching the rays chase fish around the bay as the sun set.  
I started with the tasty crab and corn chowder but was a bit disappointed with al dente potatoes in the bowl. 
Wife ordered the scallops which were superb as was my crab stuffed grouper. But my rice was also inadequately cooked. 
Creve brûlée was excellent as was Tim's attentive service. 
Worth going again, but they need to get all the parts of the dishes correct to get 5 stars.
Improve this in GPT way:
In the realm of culinary adventures, my long-lost friend and I embarked on a delightful double date for an evening of relaxation. To our surprise, we discovered that securing a reservation before 8 o'clock proved quite the challenge during the early days of August. Undeterred by this minor setback, we decided to arrive an hour ahead of schedule and indulge in libations at the captivating lobby while the skillful piano man serenaded us with his enchanting melodies. Although the bartender initially operated at a leisurely pace, he eventually made it his mission to ensure our glasses were perpetually brimming with satisfaction.

Eventually, the time arrived when our table, nestled comfortably in the corner and boasting a splendid view through the glass, awaited our presence ahead of schedule. As the sun gracefully bid adieu and painted the sky with its vibrant hues, we relished the spectacle of rays playfully pursuing their piscine companions across the tranquil bay.

To embark upon our culinary voyage, I opted to commence with a delectable bowl of crab and corn chowder. Nevertheless, my palate was slightly disheartened by the presence of al dente potatoes within the savory concoction. Conversely, my beloved wife delighted in a plate of exquisitely executed scallops, their flavors dancing jubilantly upon her discerning taste buds. Meanwhile, I savored the succulent crab-stuffed grouper, which proclaimed itself as a true masterpiece of culinary prowess. Regrettably, however, the accompanying rice failed to meet my expectations, undercooked and slightly lacking in texture.

Ending our epicurean odyssey on a sweet note, we indulged in a flawless crème brûlée that left an indelible mark upon our palates. Accompanying this impressive gastronomic experience, Tim, our attentive server, exhibited unparalleled dedication and professionalism.

In light of this memorable dining venture, we confidently conclude that a return visit is warranted. However, in order to achieve the pinnacle of gastronomic brilliance worthy of a perfect rating, it is imperative for every facet of their culinary creations to be executed flawlessly.

Cozy and family friendly restaurant. I came here for a private engagement party, where the bride and groom to be had arranged for special menus and baked all of their desserts. There were a few booth tables reserved for presents, wine, and desserts. No room for side tables like in an actual special events space.

The wait staff was nice. From the limited menu, I picked the Penne Fellini, which has prosciutto di parma, peas, onions, and light cream sauce. The whole dish was literally this pasta swimming in sauce. It may have had a light cream flavor, but it was ladled heavily onto the pasta. I didn't have a desire to consume an entire meal of this, so I ended up not finishing.

It was a fun celebration, and we were really there for the friends and family, not the food. Oh, and we also had the bruschetta and salad, neither of which was very memorable. I wouldn't be thrilled to come back here, but I think it's awesome that they turned the whole restaurant into a venue for such a special occasion!

input:
FOOD REVIEW

If you're looking for quality meal that is quick and affordable, the Fountain has you covered. The menu isn't extensive, but it's got a good amount of inexpensive sandwiches, salads, and soups.  

Their Cuban Sandwich ($10 w/ side) was pretty excellent.  The bread wasn't the traditional panini-style, but a French baguette...it was still great and had a little crispness to it.  All the main ingredients (meat, mustard, pickles, cheese) were in good balance.  As a Florida boy who loves his Cuban sandwiches, I would definitely recommend this.

I also tried a bit of their Royal Grille, a grilled-chese sandwich with several cheeses, as well as apple slices, on whole grain wheat bread ($8.50 w/ side, extra to add ham/turkey).  It was damn good and hit the grilled cheese craving just right.  A side salad was also done well.

For my side, I chose their "spicy carrots" which sounded unique.  It consists of sliced raw carrots that have been marinated in a tangy dressing with crushed red pepper, served in a cup. The carrots were cold and crisp and the flavors were fantastic.  The spice was just enough to be pleasant.  I would definitely get these again.

Our food came out super quick and our service was great.  I'm looking forward to trying a couple more items and bumping this up to 5 stars.
Improve this in GPT way:
If you're in need of a quick and affordable meal without compromising on quality, look no further than the Fountain. While the menu isn't extensive, it offers a satisfying variety of inexpensive sandwiches, salads, and soups.

One standout item is their Cuban Sandwich ($10 with a side). It deviates from the traditional panini-style bread, opting for a French baguette instead. Surprisingly, this change works wonderfully, adding a delightful crispness to the sandwich. The combination of meat, mustard, pickles, and cheese is perfectly balanced. As someone hailing from Florida and a lover of Cuban sandwiches, I wholeheartedly recommend this option.

Another dish worth mentioning is their Royal Grille, a grilled-cheese sandwich prepared with a medley of cheeses and accompanied by apple slices, all between slices of whole grain wheat bread ($8.50 with a side, extra charges for ham/turkey). This creation satisfies any grilled cheese craving with finesse. Additionally, the side salad served alongside the sandwich is executed flawlessly.

As for my chosen side dish, I opted for the "spicy carrots," a unique offering. It features thinly sliced raw carrots marinated in a tangy dressing infused with crushed red pepper. Served refreshingly cold and delightfully crisp, these carrots burst with fantastic flavors. The spiciness is perfectly balanced, making each bite pleasant and memorable. Without a doubt, I would reorder this side dish.

Not only did our food arrive promptly, but the service we received was also exceptional. I eagerly anticipate trying a few more items from their menu and have no doubt that a five-star rating awaits.

input:
Burger Up is, by far, one of our favorite restaurants in the Nashville area.  It has a cool hipster vibe, without being annoying :)  The burgers are outstanding, and there are endless options, whether you prefer beef, chicken, seafood, or veggie!  I would recommend the Woodstock - the Jack Daniels Maple Ketchup is out of this world, and Benton's bacon is always delicious.  Upgrade to the truffle fries; they're to die for.  Or, if you're a vegetarian, the troyathalon is a great option.  Filling, with great texture and flavor.  As far as drinks go, 12 South Lemonade.

The customer service is also great.  They've always been attentive, but not "on top of you", and they're very knowledgable about their food.  Parking can be a bit difficult at certain times of the day, but it's worth a short walk if necessary.

I would definitely recommend checking it out!

input:
Great Mexican BYOB! I went to Las Cazuelas for the first time for my birthday.  We had a wonderful time.  I was looking for a fun and festive place to go with friends.  This was the perfect choice. We brought our own bottle of tequila, and they made tasty margaritas for the table.  Those were a big hit with my friends, and a cool twist for a Mexican BYOB.  The restaurant is cute.  Plus, the food here is delicious. 

I'm surprised this place doesn't have higher reviews on Yelp, because it far exceeded my expectations... 

The guacamole appetizer was fresh and yummy.  I ordered the shrimp entree with rice and vegetables, and asked for it spicy.  My entrée had an attractive presentation on the plate (i.e. looked classy), and was delicious, well seasoned, and very fresh. On my suggestion, my partner ordered one of their mole sauce dishes (i.e. a sauce usually made from unsweetened chocolate and pureed pumpkin seeds), and it was tasty too. 

I should also note that the waitress was very attentive.  When I placed my order, I explained to her that I have mild lactose intolerance and can't eat much butter or cream (but am okay with cheese), so she had the chef cook the veggies in olive oil, rather than butter.  Thanks for being so cool about accommodating that request!  

The prices are extremely reasonable for fancy and unusual Mexican food, and I love the fact they're a BYOB.  The chef serves creative and inspired cuisine, which has a traditional flair and style to it.  In other words: Don't come here for regular tacos or burritos.  Come here for a fun foodie experience at a reasonable price, and bring tequila for the perk of BYOB Margaritas!

The ambiance was lively and festive, creating a fun atmosphere for our gathering. The unique twist of being a Mexican BYOB made it even more enjoyable. We brought a bottle of tequila and the restaurant's skilled bartenders prepared delicious margaritas for the entire table, which was a hit with everyone.

The restaurant itself has a charming and cozy vibe, adding to the overall experience. However, the real star of the show was the food. The guacamole appetizer was incredibly fresh and had a rich flavor. For my main course, I opted for the shrimp entree with rice and vegetables, requesting it to be spicy. The presentation was visually appealing, and the dish itself was flavorful, well-seasoned, and made with top-notch ingredients. I also suggested that my partner try one of their mole sauce dishes, which had a delicious combination of unsweetened chocolate and pureed pumpkin seeds.

What impressed me further was the attentive and accommodating waitress. I informed her about my mild lactose intolerance and she made sure the chef cooked the vegetables in olive oil instead of butter, which was greatly appreciated.

Considering the quality of the food and the overall dining experience, Las Cazuelas' prices are surprisingly reasonable. It's worth noting that this is not your average Mexican restaurant, as they serve creative and inspired cuisine with a traditional flair. If you're looking for regular tacos or burritos, this might not be the place for you. However, if you're seeking a unique and enjoyable foodie experience at an affordable price, along with the added perk of being a BYOB establishment, Las Cazuelas is a must-visit.

input:
I'm not really sure why I bother going to other restaurants. 

Every Valentine's Day I try to find some cute, new little BYO for me and my boyfriend to try out and I spend weeks scouring menus and Yelp reviews. 

Every year SOMETHING goes wrong and I get frustrated and pissed off and he always says "Let's go to Jones".

This year was no different. We went out last night (2/12/11...the weekend before Valentines Day) to the BYO I picked out and when I made our reservations, no mention was made that they had a special fixed menu that night consisting SOLELY of seafood, which I am allergic to. As I started to get upset at our table, my boyfriend said "Let's go to Jones".

We got there, were told there was a little bit of a wait, so we sat at the bar for a drink. About 5-10 minutes later they came and got us and sat us at our table. Our waiter (who was WONDERFUL and looked like Jared Leto - extra bonus-) came over and took our order and the food came out perfectly (as usual) and right on time.

We both got the filet, done rare and the spinach it came with was fantastic. The mac and cheese is also an app we get every time and is one of my favorites. I got the deviled eggs for the first time and holy crap they were amazing. I'm gonna say, possibly the best ones I've ever had (sorry, Dad). 

Everything about this restaurant leans towards comfort and it's always done so well. The atmosphere, the staff, the decor, the food, hell even the temperature. I've never had a bad experience at Jones and I don't think I ever will. 

Next year....we'll just go straight to Jones.

The sour cream and guacamole were fresh, but the entrees were just average at best.  The quesadillas had too much cheese and not much else flavor.  

The meal was not bad, but there are better options close by.

My only drawbacks are:  no teeth cleaning; the price is the same regardless if the dog is 5 lbs or 40 lbs; and the feeling of judgement for not taking better care of my dogs (but that could just be me).

I was just passing through Tuscon. Native American inspired breakfast food? I just had to have some :-).  Basically I ended up with amazing and unique food that I wish I could have everyday! Five stars!

It took me while to decide what I wanted because there was so many things I wanted. 

Finally, I ended up with the pueblo, which basically is the green corn waffle with eggs the way you want it and a choice of a side (I got chorizo). The waiter told me how to eat it: put the syrup + hot sauce on the waffle and enjoy. But, instead, I ended up making an awesome syrup, hot sauce, egg, chorizo and red sauce tower on my waffle for each bite. It was delicious - try it!!!
Improve this in GPT way:
My recent visit to Tuscon led me to discover a delightful Native American-inspired breakfast dish that left me truly yearning for more! With so many tempting options to choose from, it took me a while to settle on my selection.

In the end, I opted for the pueblo, a delectable green corn waffle accompanied by eggs prepared to my liking. As if that weren't enough, I had the pleasure of selecting a side dish, and I couldn't resist the tantalizing appeal of chorizo. The knowledgeable waiter kindly instructed me on savoring this culinary masterpiece: drizzle the waffle with both syrup and hot sauce, and simply relish the symphony of flavors. However, I couldn't resist taking it a step further.

What ensued was a delightful experiment in gastronomy as I built a magnificent tower upon my waffle, consisting of syrup, hot sauce, eggs, chorizo, and a generous helping of red sauce. Each bite was an explosion of harmonious tastes that left me in awe. I implore you to try this extraordinary combination for yourself; trust me, it's a culinary adventure you won't regret. A true feast for the senses deserving of a resounding five-star rating!

input:
This shop is a slice of Disney beauty and magic hiding on the edge of Broad Ripple, and a MUST stop of sweets, treats, and dreaminess. Your Instagram needs this place. Hands down the ~best~ red velvet cake of my life.

Appearance: The Cake Bake Shop is a beautifully decorated, small white house with a captivating design. The flowers around the sign make it an #instaworthy post for sure, and when the weather is nice, the outdoor seating must be gorgeous.

Inside the Cake Shop will take your breath away, light airy colors and flowers and twinkling lights. This isn't the kind of cake shop you do take-out at, you'll want to sit and enjoy. 

Food: I wanted to try the Raspberry Champagne cake, unfortunately one wouldn't be ready for a little while, so I ordered a slice of the Red Velvet  Cake. The floral icing work was so perfect I didn't want to touch it, but I had to because come on it's cake. What I assume must have been cream cheese filling in the middle was decadent and I never wanted the cake to end. ***I felt one slice was plenty for two people, it's HUGE

I was torn between the Rose Cappuccino and the Lavender Latte. I went with the Lavender Latte, hot, and it was stunning, it was a creamy, smooth, not-at-all bitter latte and the hint of lavender was enough to taste but not over powering, it was probably the most perfect coffee I've ever had in my life. 

Price: the coffee is pricy, $6, so not a regular coffee stop for me, but for #treatyoself it's the way to go. The slice of cake was $12 but like I mentioned, it was enough for two people and for how amazing it was, I think it's so worth it.

Customer Service: I mentioned Disney initially because the friendliness, care, and attention of the staff felt just like Disney. They were kind, they helped me decide what to try, and the barista even offered to make me the rose cappuccino if I didn't like the lavender latte after trying it - how sweet! 

I will most definitely think to come here if anyone visits and wants something sweet. This place has my heart and is a hidden gem to anyone who has a sweet tooth!

Check out my #FirstTimeFriday highlight of my visit to The Cake Bake Shop on my Instagram @jordanqjordanq for pictures of everything mentioned above!

I eat at Sukho Thai quite a bit, and I don't really get the negative ratings. Is it the most authentic thai place in the area? No. Sometimes I would say they sometimes substitute certain ingredients. It is however usually pretty consistent as far as quality of food and service. 

I usually get the red or green curry, and almost always get it "native thai hot". I have tried other things on the menu, but they are not quite as good. So I stick with what tastes good and works for me. 

The lady that owns the place is very kind and always very gracious to my wife and I. She always recognizes us and serves us promptly. She not only owns the place, but she waits all of the tables most of the time(which I think is pretty impressive). 
The place is beside a go-cart track, so that makes it a little quirky, but it's something I have grown accustomed to. 

The only thing negative I would say is that I wish they had Kee Mao on the menu, because that's my favorite. I usually go to Siam Cafe or Thai Star for that.

input:
When you dine at Muriel's, check to see if the 2nd level is open for visitors. If so, you can briefly tour the lounge area upstairs (red couches, decorative pieces). There's a wrap-around balcony where you can get a great view of Jackson Square. 

If you're curious, learn why Muriel's is haunted and find out the story behind why there's a table that is always set for two located near the stairs. 

There are two main dining rooms, a middle section (indoor patio dining area) that I personally prefer because it is quieter, and a bar area located at the back near the restrooms. I love the indoor patio dining area because it brings a bit of the outdoors in a quiet indoor setting. 

On my first visit, I ordered from the dinner pre-fix menu which is a great deal (appetizer or soup + entrée + dessert = $40). The seafood gumbo soup was hearty and delicious. The dijon mustard encrusted salmon was cooked perfectly. The bread pudding was a great way to end a delicious meal.

I returned to Muriel's for lunch on another NOLA trip and tried the wood grilled pork chop. The pork chop was flavorful, tender, and moist. I was not too crazy about the red beans and rice it was served with as I found it a bit bland. The entrée was served in a bowl but should perhaps be served on a plate since it was difficult to slice the pork chop since it kept sinking into the bed of red beans and rice. 

Muriel's is one of the places I would love to return to because of the ambiance and the great food.
